items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: We made a recording together with Frank Driggs, up to Columbia

ctx.x: So he got hold of a clarinet some kind of a way, and he started to play, and everybody really dug him. Before this, mind you, he had been a big band leader all over South America, with a big band. He had made success, and all of a sudden he tripped up some kind of way and six years out of his life was gone. Now he's like coming through out of a coma, out of a sleep, and he told me, and he said that he began to put the pieces back together, and started to play.

Then he met this woman, and then she saw the great talent that he had, and then she kind of put him back on his feet. And then him and his daughter -- he started pushing her, and whatnot, and then she became a big star. They worked together. He was singing like Pops, and he did the thing, he came to New York. We made a recording together with Frank Driggs, up to Columbia, and we recorded 13th and Lydia, the place that I was talking about in the interview with Milt.
